title: The entangled Born correlations: a mixed-state entanglement witness through the Born rule forced on the composite algebra
abstract: Kernel-checked entanglement package on the bipartite matrix algebra (2x2 tensor 2x2, native product index): (1) the separable-state CHSH bound 2 for the real-Pauli tuple, proved through the Bloch-disk constraint with no spectral theory; (2) an entanglement witness — a bipartite state, positive semidefinite with unit trace, that is NOT separable, with Born CHSH expectation equal to the Tsirelson value 2*sqrt(2) (the Bell state, exhibited explicitly in the Solution); (3) spectral projections without spectral theory — (1+W)/2 is an effect for every Hermitian involution W, any finite dimension; (4) the two-party correlation law forced, not postulated: for any state representing a generalized probability measure on effects (Busch's theorem vocabulary; no continuity assumed), the correlation at any pair of binary-observable settings is an explicit difference of the measure's values at two effects; (5) the assembly — a state that is not separable, is the UNIQUE state reproducing its own effect statistics (Born-rule uniqueness on the composite algebra), attains the Tsirelson value, and carries the witness correlation table XX = ZZ = 1, XZ = ZX = 0. Extended (second session, 2026-08-31) by five further compared theorems — the general bounds and the quantitative Werner-family layer: (6) the separable bound 2 at ARBITRARY finite local dimensions and arbitrary Hermitian-involution settings; (7) the state-level Tsirelson bound 2*sqrt(2) at the same generality; (8) the Werner family W_p = p|Phi+><Phi+| + ((1-p)/4)1, spelled inline from the explicit Bell projector, has CHSH expectation at most 2*sqrt(2)*p at any Hermitian-involution settings with traceless party-1 observables (p >= 0) — the Werner line of the Horodecki 1995 criterion; (9) the violation threshold: for p >= 0, W_p violates CHSH at some such settings iff p > 1/sqrt(2); (10) the separability endpoint (Werner 1989): W_p is separable for 0 <= p <= 1/3. All hypotheses are inline; the compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.trace, the Kronecker product, Real.sqrt, Matrix.vecMulVec) with no custom definitions.
